stimuli.text: A block of mass 4 kg on a 30° incline is connected by a light string over a light, frictionless pulley at the top of the incline to a hanging block of mass 8 kg. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the incline is 0.1. The system is released from rest, and the hanging block descends.
A block of mass 1.5 kg on a horizontal frictionless surface is attached to a spring. Its position is $$x(t) = 0.13\cos(10t)$$, with x in meters and t in seconds.
Students measure the period of a simple pendulum for several string lengths, using small amplitudes.
A hoop (I = MR²) and a solid cylinder (I = ½MR²) of equal mass M and radius R are released from rest at the top of the same ramp of height 0.7 m. Both roll without slipping.

questions.stem: A 4 kg cart moving at 5 m/s collides with and sticks to a 5 kg cart at rest. What is their speed after the collision?

options.why: Kinetic energy is not conserved here.
Use m₁v₁ for the initial momentum.
Correct. Momentum is conserved; kinetic energy is not.

questions.explanation: v_f = 4·5/9 = 2.22 m/s; kinetic energy lost = 27.8 J.

questions.stem: A 0.3 kg ball hits a wall at 14 m/s and rebounds at 4 m/s. The contact lasts 0.03 s. What is the average force from the wall?

options.why: The velocity reverses, so the speeds add.
Correct. Δp = m(v_f − v_i) with the direction reversed.

questions.stem: A particle's position is $$x(t) = -2t^3 - 6t^2 - 2t$$, with x in meters and t in seconds. What is its acceleration at $$t = 3$$ s?

options.why: Bring each exponent down as a factor when differentiating.
That is the velocity; differentiate again.
The derivative of 2bt is 2b, which also remains.

questions.explanation: a(t) = -12t - 12, so at t = 3 the value is -48.

questions.stem: A block slides down a 20° incline. The coefficient of kinetic friction is 0.3. What is the magnitude of its acceleration?

options.why: The component along the incline is mg sin θ.
Friction depends on the normal force, mg cos θ.
Correct. a = g(sin θ − μk cos θ).

questions.stem: Two springs with constants 80 N/m and 80 N/m are connected in parallel and support a 3 kg mass at rest. How far do they stretch in total?

options.why: The force is the weight, mg.
Series and parallel rules are reversed.

questions.stem: A ball rolls off a horizontal ledge 13 m high at 2 m/s. How far from the base of the ledge does it land?

options.why: Correct. Fall time from the height, times the horizontal speed.
Horizontal and vertical motion are independent.
Take the square root for the time.

questions.stem: A motor lifts a 240 kg load 16 m at constant speed in 4 s. What average power does it deliver?

options.why: That is the work; divide by time.

questions.stem: A wheel spinning at 44 rad/s slows uniformly to rest in 19 s. How many revolutions does it make while stopping?

options.why: The average angular speed is ω₀/2.
Correct. Δθ = ½ω₀t, then divide by 2π.
That is in radians; convert to revolutions.

questions.stem: A force $$F(x) = 6x^2$$ N acts along the x-axis. How much work does it do on an object moving from $$x = 2$$ m to $$x = 4$$ m?

options.why: Integrate; do not just evaluate F.

questions.stem: A motor lifts a 450 kg load 16 m at constant speed in 21 s. What average power does it deliver?

options.why: That is the work; divide by time.

questions.stem: A planet has 4 times Earth's mass and 0.5 times Earth's radius. What is the gravitational field strength at its surface? (Earth's is 9.8 N/kg.)
A simple pendulum is 0.6 m long. What is its period for small oscillations?
A spring with $$k = 410$$ N/m is compressed 0.19 m and launches a 0.3 kg block across a frictionless surface. What is the block's speed after leaving the spring?

options.why: The ½ appears on both sides.

questions.stem: Masses of 4 kg and 3 kg hang on either side of a light, frictionless pulley. What is the tension in the string?

options.why: The heavier mass accelerates down, so T is less than its weight.
The lighter mass accelerates up, so T exceeds its weight.

questions.stem: A system obeys $$\frac{d^2x}{dt^2} = -81x$$. What is the period of its motion?

options.why: ω is the square root of the coefficient.

questions.stem: The potential energy of a particle is $$U(x) = 3x^3 - 33x$$ J. At what positive x is the particle in stable equilibrium?

options.why: Correct. Equilibrium where dU/dx = 0; stable at a minimum.
Set the derivative, not U, to zero.

questions.explanation: dU/dx = 9x² − 33 = 0 gives x = 1.91 m; d²U/dx² > 0 there, so it is stable.

questions.stem: A constant torque of 16 N·m acts on a wheel ($$I = 1.2$$ kg·m²) initially at rest, through 9 revolutions. What is the wheel's final angular speed?

options.why: Correct. Work τΔθ (in radians) equals ½Iω².

questions.stem: An object's acceleration is $$a(t) = 1t$$ m/s². At $$t = 0$$ it has velocity 6 m/s and is at $$x = 0$$. What is its velocity at $$t = 5$$ s?

options.why: The acceleration is not constant, so constant-acceleration equations do not apply.
Correct. Integrate a(t) and add the initial velocity.

questions.stem: A uniform disk of mass 8 kg and radius 0.4 m rotates about an axis perpendicular to it, 0.5 m from its center. What is its rotational inertia?

options.why: Correct. Parallel-axis theorem: I = ½MR² + Md².
The axis is not through the center.
Include the disk's own I about its center.

questions.stem: A 90 kg person stands on a scale in an elevator that is accelerating upward at 2 m/s². What does the scale read?

options.why: The acceleration changes the normal force.
Correct. The scale reads the normal force: N − mg = ma (up positive).
Check the direction of the acceleration.

questions.stem: Satellite B orbits a planet in a circular orbit 3 times the radius of satellite A's circular orbit. What is the ratio of B's orbital speed to A's?
A ball is launched from level ground at 22 m/s at 37° above the horizontal. Ignoring air resistance, what is its maximum height?

options.why: Use the vertical component, v₀ sin θ.
Correct. Treat horizontal and vertical motion separately.

questions.explanation: v₀x = 17.6 m/s, v₀y = 13.2 m/s. H = v₀y²/(2g) = 8.94 m.

questions.stem: A 3 kg object at rest experiences a net force $$F(t) = 10t$$ N from $$t = 0$$ to $$t = 3$$ s. What is its final speed?

options.why: Divide by the mass to get speed.
Correct. Impulse ∫F dt equals the change in momentum.

questions.explanation: J = ∫F dt = 45 N·s; v = J/m = 15 m/s.

questions.stem: A solid sphere rolls without slipping from rest down a ramp of height 2.8 m. What is its speed at the bottom?

options.why: Correct. mgh = ½mv²(1 + β) with I = ⅖MR².
That is only correct for a hoop.

questions.stem: A 0.5 kg mass oscillates on a spring with $$k = 165$$ N/m. What is the period?
A boat points straight across a river 60 m wide, moving at 3 m/s relative to the water. The current flows at 1 m/s. How far downstream does the boat land?

options.why: Correct. The current does not change the time to cross; it only carries the boat downstream.
That is a time, not a distance.

questions.stem: Satellite B orbits a planet in a circular orbit 16 times the radius of satellite A's circular orbit. What is the ratio of B's orbital speed to A's?
A 1500 kg car heading east at 7 m/s collides with a 2500 kg car heading north at 19 m/s, and they lock together. What is their speed just after the collision?

options.why: Momentum is a vector; add components at right angles.
Weight each velocity by its mass.
Correct. Conserve momentum in x and y separately, then combine.

questions.stem: A 7 kg block on a horizontal table is connected by a string over a light pulley to a hanging 3 kg block. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the table and the block is 0.3. What is the acceleration of the blocks?

options.why: Correct. Net force (m₂g − μm₁g) divided by the total mass.
Include friction on the table block.

questions.stem: A uniform rod of length 2 m is pivoted at one end and released from rest in a horizontal position. What is its angular acceleration just after release?

options.why: Correct. τ = Mg(L/2) and I = ML²/3 give α = 3g/(2L).
Use τ = Iα with I = ML²/3.

questions.stem: A planet has mass $$1 \times 10^{23}$$ kg and radius $$4 \times 10^{7}$$ m. What is the escape speed from its surface? ($$G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11}$$ N·m²/kg²)

options.why: That is the circular orbit speed; escape needs √2 times more.

questions.stem: A 1 kg mass hangs from a light string wrapped around a uniform disk pulley of mass 7 kg that turns on a frictionless axle. What is the acceleration of the mass?

options.why: The pulley's inertia reduces the acceleration.
Correct. a = mg/(m + M/2), using I = ½MR² and a = Rα.

questions.explanation: mg − T = ma and TR = ½MR²(a/R) give a = 2.18 m/s².

questions.stem: A 2 kg ball on a 1.3 m string moves in a vertical circle. At the bottom of the circle its speed is 5 m/s. What is the tension in the string there?

options.why: Check the direction of gravity relative to the center.
Correct. At the bottom, T − mg = mv²/r.

questions.stem: A block starts from rest and slides 8 m down a 20° incline with coefficient of kinetic friction 0.3. What is its speed at the bottom?

options.why: Use the vertical drop, L sin θ.
Friction depends on the normal force, mg cos θ.
Correct. mgh − μmg cos θ·L = ½mv².

questions.stem: An object of mass 1.2 kg falls from rest with a drag force $$F = -bv$$, where $$b = 0.02$$ kg/s. What is its terminal speed?

options.why: Correct. At terminal speed, mg = bv.
Drag here is linear in v.

questions.explanation: v_T = mg/b = 588 m/s and τ = m/b = 60 s.

questions.stem: A rod lies along the x-axis from $$x = 0$$ to $$x = 6$$ m and has linear mass density $$\lambda = kx^3$$. Where is its center of mass?

options.why: The exponents are n + 2 and n + 1.

questions.stem: A uniform 7 m beam weighing 500 N rests on supports at both ends. A 600 N load sits 4 m from the left end. What force does the right support exert?

options.why: Include the beam's weight at its center.
Correct. Take torques about the left support.
That is the left support's force.
The load is not at the center.

questions.stem: A mass on a spring oscillates with angular frequency 11 rad/s and amplitude 0.06 m. What is its speed when it is 0.006 m from equilibrium?

options.why: That is the maximum speed, at x = 0.
Correct. v = ω√(A² − x²), from conservation of energy.
Use A² − x² under a square root.
Speed is greatest at equilibrium, not at the ends.

questions.stem: A 1 kg ball moving at +5 m/s collides elastically head-on with a 3 kg ball at rest. What is the velocity of the 3 kg ball afterward (positive in the original direction)?

options.why: Correct. Elastic: conserve momentum and kinetic energy (relative velocity reverses).
That would be a sticking collision.

questions.explanation: v₁' = (m₁ − m₂)v/(m₁ + m₂) = -2.5 m/s; v₂' = 2m₁v/(m₁ + m₂) = 2.5 m/s.

questions.stem: A 10 g bullet moving at 350 m/s embeds in a 3.6 kg block hanging from strings. How high does the block rise?

options.why: Kinetic energy is not conserved in the collision.
Correct. Momentum for the collision, then energy for the swing.
Find the block's speed after the collision first.

questions.explanation: V = 0.97 m/s after the collision; h = V²/(2g) = 0.048 m.

questions.title: Block on an incline with a hanging mass

parts.prompt: Draw (describe) a free-body diagram for the 4 kg block, labeling each force.

rubric.criterion: Weight down, normal force perpendicular to the incline, tension up the incline.
Kinetic friction down the incline (opposite the motion).

parts.prompt: Derive an expression for the acceleration of the system in terms of the masses, θ, μ and g, then calculate its value.

rubric.criterion: Newton's second law applied to each block (or the system).

parts.prompt: Calculate the tension in the string.
Calculate the speed of the blocks after the hanging block has descended 2 m, and the work done by friction on the incline block during that motion.

rubric.criterion: Work by friction, with a negative sign.

parts.prompt: Sketch (describe) graphs of position, velocity and acceleration versus time for one period, aligned vertically.

rubric.criterion: Position is a cosine starting at +A; velocity is a negative sine starting at 0.
rubric.example: x starts at 0.13 m; v starts at 0 and goes negative.

rubric.criterion: Acceleration starts at its negative maximum and is opposite in sign to position throughout.

parts.prompt: Derive expressions for v(t) and a(t), and determine the maximum speed and maximum acceleration.
Calculate the spring constant and the period.
Calculate the total mechanical energy and describe how kinetic and potential energy vary during one period.

rubric.example: K is maximum at x = 0 and zero at x = ±A; U is the reverse; the sum is constant. Each varies twice per period.

parts.prompt: Describe a procedure the students could use to measure the period accurately, including how to reduce uncertainty.

rubric.example: Time 10 swings with a stopwatch and divide by 10.

rubric.criterion: Keep the amplitude small and repeat trials.
rubric.example: Release from under about 10° and average several trials.

parts.prompt: Identify quantities to graph that would give a straight line, and explain how g can be found from the graph.
Plot (describe) the linearized data and draw a best-fit line. Use it to calculate an experimental value of g.
The students repeat the experiment with a much larger amplitude. Predict how the measured periods would change and explain.

rubric.criterion: Periods increase slightly; the small-angle approximation (sin θ ≈ θ) no longer holds.
rubric.example: The restoring torque is less than proportional to θ at large angles.

parts.prompt: Without calculating, predict which object reaches the bottom first. Justify your prediction using energy.

rubric.example: It has the smaller rotational inertia per MR².

rubric.criterion: Justification: less of its energy goes into rotation, so more is translational kinetic energy.

parts.prompt: Derive an expression for the speed at the bottom of an object with rotational inertia βMR², in terms of g, h and β.

rubric.criterion: Energy conservation including both forms of kinetic energy, with v = Rω.

parts.prompt: Calculate the speed of each object at the bottom.
Explain whether your derived expression is consistent with your prediction in part (a), and why neither speed depends on M or R.

rubric.criterion: Smaller β gives larger v, consistent with the prediction.
M and R cancel in the energy equation.
rubric.example: Only the shape factor β matters.
